attribution.note: Marcus's own commentary on the Zero Hedge chart, in his own voice.

semantics.note: It keeps the comparison to the two rightmost bars and the point that they show revenue. It is a present-tense observation.

contract.note: Reading 'recent increase' as the publication-week gain fits the nearby 'up nearly 50% this week'. A single-day reading would change the result, so the interpretation is decisive.

evidence.note: Oracle's own guidance gives $114B and $144B (sum $258B) for the last two forecast years. Without the chart, these can't be confirmed as its rightmost bars.
Gives a $244B gain for one trading day only. That is not the weekly interval the contract uses.

reviews.rationale: The chart was never retrieved, so its final two bars are unverified. No consistent weekly market-cap change with a pre-publication endpoint was established. The single-day $244B figure is below $258B but doesn't match the contract's weekly reading. Neither condition can be confirmed.

attribution.note: The 'In short' summary and the 'spoiler alert' aside are in Marcus's own voice.

semantics.note: It keeps both parts: that OpenAI thought or claimed GPT-5 would be tantamount to AGI, and that it wasn't.

contract.note: The ordinary reading of AGI as broadly human-level general capability is fair. Requiring a GPT-5-specific expectation from OpenAI matches what Marcus actually wrote.

evidence.note: Guardian report from launch day: Altman admitted GPT-5 had not reached AGI. Supports the not-AGI part only.
The August 2025 preprint finds GPT-5 below human performance on many spatial tasks. Supports substantial limitations, but it is not a full AGI test.

reviews.rationale: The not-AGI part is well supported by Altman's launch admission and the independent study. The other part, that OpenAI thought or claimed GPT-5 would be tantamount to AGI, has no verified supporting statement. The support condition needs both parts, so it is not met. Not finding a statement is not a contradiction, so the overall result is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: It is correctly narrowed to the OpenAI contracts under discussion, and it keeps both parts: the chips and the cash.

contract.note: Treating 'cash' as cash and cash equivalents at quarter-end is an ordinary reading, with borrowing treated as separate context. That reading is fair.

evidence.note: Oracle's filing shows $10.4B in cash and equivalents at Aug 31, 2025. It gives no cost for the missing chips to compare against.
OpenAI's disclosure describes 4.5GW still under development, with some racks already delivered. It gives neither Oracle's chip inventory nor the purchase cost.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows Oracle's cash balance but not the chips the contracts require, Oracle's existing inventory, or the cost of the shortfall. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition can be checked.
